page: The Vultr vbm-6c-32gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server powered by a 6-core, 12-thread AMD EPYC 4245P processor running at a base clock speed of 3.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources are fully dedicated with no hypervisor layer overhead, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for modern vector instructions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions. System memory is configured at 32.0 GB of RAM, paired directly with a single 1920 GB local NVMe SSD and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server does not include a dedicated GPU accelerator.

Benchmark evaluations reveal exceptional single-core processing capabilities, with both stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests placing the instance in the top tier of performance. Single-threaded data tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core throughput across stress-ng and Geekbench falls in the median range due to the 6-core hardware limitation. Passmark memory testing demonstrates top-tier efficiency, though uncached large-block sequential memory write bandwidth drops into the lower quartile at 23.57 GB/s. Static web throughput, Redis operations, and software compilation perform solidly within standard mid-range benchmarks.

From an infrastructure perspective, this bare metal profile provides a cost-effective alternative to multi-tenant virtual machines by removing CPU steal and virtualization performance penalties. The trade-off centers on lower parallel scaling and memory density relative to large enterprise nodes, balanced by superior single-thread responsiveness and low latency. The Vultr vbm-6c-32gb-amd is suited for compute-focused applications requiring high clock speeds, fast local NVMe transactions, continuous integration pipelines, small-model edge inference, and dedicated web application hosting.
description: The Vultr vbm-6c-32gb-amd is a single-socket bare metal server featuring a 6-core, 12-thread AMD EPYC 4245P processor running at 3.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture with dedicated hardware execution. The platform is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, an onboard 1920 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage, and one public IPv4 address, operating without GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, the system delivers top-tier single-core CPU execution, leading single-threaded compression throughput, and high memory benchmark scores. Multi-threaded processing and static web workloads remain in the median range, constrained by the physical core count, alongside moderate uncached memory write bandwidth. This server represents an efficient deployment target for single-thread bound processes, CI/CD compilation tasks, light database hosting, and high-frequency backend API services.
